articles.title: UFC Fighter Josh Hokit Has No Regrets About Michelle Obama Verbal Attack
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — UFC heavyweight Josh Hokit said he has no regrets about using the White House as a bully pulpit to make an extraordinary and unfounded attack based on a right-wing conspiracy theory about former first lady Michelle Obama.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — UFC heavyweight Josh Hokit said he has no regrets about using the White House as a bully pulpit to make an extraordinary and unfounded attack based on a right-wing conspiracy theory about former first lady Michelle Obama.

Hokit made his vulgar remarks inside the octagon in June after winning his fight at the UFC event to mark President Donald Trump's 80th birthday on the South Lawn of the White House.

Hokit fights for the first time since then on Saturday when he challenges heavyweight champion Cyril Gane in the main event of UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden.

Hokit again made a series of crass insults about other fighters on the fight card on Wednesday inside a New York hotel before taking questions about his championship bout and his remarks on Obama.

"I'll never look back and be like, I regret that," Hokit said.

Wearing a black stocking cap over an American flag bandana, sunglasses and fight gloves, Hokit said he "took the rap of a villain" before he burst into what he called a freestyle rap to express his lack of regret.

Hokit said he was "sure it wasn't" the right thing to do to insult the former First Lady but was proud the remarks had put his image on Trump's Truth Social posts. In one post, Hokit appeared in cartoon form alongside UFC chief Dana White in the White House briefing room.

Trump said over the weekend he had offered White the job of White House press secretary. White declined the frivolous offer.

"I'm here to take what's mine," Hokit said. "If I've got to rub some people the wrong way, if I've got to say some (stuff) in the wrong location, it is what it is. Was it not a good location to say it? I mean, we're at the White House. That house represents freedom of speech. So it is what it is. I think it was the perfect location to say it."

The 28-year-old Hokit is 10-0 in his MMA career and has won all six fights since joining UFC in 2025.

articles.title: AEW Dynamite, Collision Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights Before Full Gear
articles.summary: Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of AEW Dynamite and Collision on November 11.
articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of AEW Dynamite and Collision on November 11.

Here is a look at what AEW advertised for the go-home show before Full Gear this weekend:

FTR vs. MCMG (Final match in Best of 5 Series)

Jay White and Mercedes Mone vs. Jon Moxley and Marina Shafir

Tommaso Ciampa vs. Mike Bailey (National Championship)

Let's take a look at everything that happened on this week's combined Dynamite and Collision.

The show started with a Blood and Guts recap video before we saw a video of Will Ospreay talking to the team after last week's loss. Adam Copeland explained why he submitted before storming off.

The first segment of the night was the face-to-face meeting between Kyle Fletcher and Will Ospreay ahead of their world title match this weekend at Full Gear.

Fletcher reminded the crowd that this is the arena where he revealed his shaved head, which prompted a "You look stupid" chant from the fans.

The Protostar said Ospreay is responsible for setting him on this journey, and he actually thanked him, but when Will sounded sincere in his response, Fletcher said he misunderstood and listed all of the violent things he would do to Ospreay again if he had the chance.

The champ talked about Fletcher being responsible for the worst 10 months of his career before saying he is going to fight like his life is on the line at Full Gear. After some poking and prodding, Fletcher angrily admitted he was jealous of Ospreay.

This was much longer than most AEW talking segments, but that was not a bad thing. Fletcher and Ospreay had the crowd invested the entire time, and their years of shared history helped add to the drama.

Fletcher is absolutely a future world champion, and it wouldn't be surprising to see that happen this weekend. He carried this segment and actually elevated Ospreay on the mic. He sold every emotional beat perfectly. The way he promised to take everything from Ospreay was terrific.

This was one of the better AEW promo segments in recent memory.

Copeland seemed to have doubts about his place in AEW.

Fletcher is low-key one of the funnier people in AEW. If he ever turns babyface, he could become very popular with his sense of humor.

Bandido and Brody King were hoping to gain some momentum with a win over New Level before their trios title defense at Full Gear against them and Swerve Strickland.

Kofi and Austin Creed wasted no time and attacked King and Bandido during their entrance. Brodido eventually gained control, and the match got started once they were all in the ring.

The feud between these teams has been elevated in recent weeks and made much more personal, and it has also elevated the trios titles to feel more important again, so this bout needed to be high-energy to keep that going ahead of the PPV.

Thankfully, AEW had three great high-flyers and one big powerhouse who were up to the task. The match ended in a double countout, but it didn't stop there. Brody and Bandido set up a table next to the ring, but their plan to put Kofi through it was thwarted at the last moment.

Kofi ended up diving off the stage and putting King through the table while Creed and Bandido brawled on the stage and took out several members of security.

A double countout is almost never the ideal ending for a match, but this is one of the rare situations where it works because it made the feud feel even more intense. The match wasn't very long, but they packed in a lot.

It was very smart to get this match started with some chaos after spending the first 30 minutes of the show on a talking segment.

The rolling fisherman's buster from Creed was an impressive display of power. He had no leverage and still picked up Bandido with ease.

The Conglomeration's Orange Cassidy took on The Cut's David Finlay in a match where everyone from their respective groups was banned from ringside.

The match started with a surprisingly quick pace for an OC bout, but he still played his usual mind games by sliding out of the ring to take a breather after a quick sequence.

Finlay played a similar game a few moments later that almost led to a double countout with neither man willing to get back into the ring until the ref was at nine with the count.

Both men really leaned into their strengths here. Finlay went for a more violent and intense offense, while Cassidy used the same semi-comedic style that has made him a popular member of the AEW roster.

This match was designed to give us a preview of Anarchy in the Arena this weekend, and while they did not have any hardcore stipulations to work with, they did a great job making this into a hard-fought contest.

Finley eventually used his shillelagh while the ref was removing a chair from the ring, and it led to him getting the win. Clark Connors hit OC with a huge Spear during some post-match shenanigans.

The Brawling Birds and WrathLander were shown having a backstage segment after Blood and Guts.

Cassidy tucking the shillelagh under the apron was funny.

The way Finlay sold the three failed suplexes was perfect.

Persephone faced a local talent this week. After losing the TBS title last week, she was hoping to make a statement.

Her opponent managed to get in exactly one move before Persephone wiped her out with her finisher for the win.

This was a typical squash. There wasn't much to it, but it's nice to see AEW keeping Persephone looking strong even without the TBS title.

Andrade had a quick interview backstage. He had his contract for a title shot framed.

The Best of Five series was about to end with the final showdown between FTR and The Motor City Machine Guns. Each team held two wins, but in addition to winning the series, the victors would receive a future shot at the tag titles.

Dax Harwood and Alex Shelley started for their teams, but it didn't take too long for Chris Sabin and Cash Wheeler to get involved. The first few minutes were controlled by MCMG, but FTR turned things around heading into the break.

The match was announced as having a 20-minute time limit before it started, so a lot of people online immediately assumed it would go to a draw and force one more match, possibly at Full Gear.

The match unfolded much like their other four bouts. It was highly competitive and made all four guys look great. Having the timekeeper announce how much time was left at various points helped build the tension.

This was one of the best matches in their series, if not the best. They had a bit of everything in this one, including a handful of moments when FTR tried to cheat, unsuccessfully.

Shockingly, the match did not end in a tie. After surviving several close calls, Shelley and Sabin scored the win Shelley hitting a sunset flip on Harwood.

Hangman and Brodido had an interview backstage to hype their Texas Death Match.

The way Shelley and Sabin work as a unit is unmatched. Even teams with actual brothers rarely work as smoothly together as them.

Wheeler used the ring bell on Sabin but it wasn't enough to put him away.

After winning the National Championship just days ago, Tommaso Ciampa already had his first title defense lined up against Mike Bailey.

They started the match with a series of chops, but Speedball took control with one swift kick to the chest.

Bailey was busted open after being sent into the steel ring steps. It didn't seem to affect him too much because it wasn't a gusher, but he still had a little blood on his face for the rest of the match.

This was a strong first title defense for Ciampa, who was hoping his national title run would go better than his TNT title run, which lasted less than two weeks.

Speedball put up a great fight, but a second running knee put him away. It's just a matter of time before Bailey has a singles title, but having Ciampa retain was the right decision.

Ilja Dragunov came out after the match to inform Ciampa that they will have a title match at Full Gear.

It's easy to forget that both Bailey and Andrade are part of United Empire now, but Speedball using the green and gold colors is a good reminder.

Ciampa being his own biggest fan will never stop being funny.

Bailey's springboard corkscrew moonsault from the top rope looked good, but he barely made contact with Ciampa because it's such an unpredictable move to attempt.

Ciampa biting Bailey's toes is the kind of thing that some fans will hate, and some fans will love, for very different reasons.

Jay White and Mercedes Mone joined forces to battle Marina Shafir and Jon Moxley from The Death Riders.

Mox and White started the match and had a nice exchange. Switchblade tried to play some mind games, but Mox was up to the challenge. The CEO tagged in, which forced Moxley to tag in Shafir, but Mone tagged out before they could make contact.

White hitting Shafir with a backbreaker and then dragging her to the corner by her hair felt like a turning point in the match. From that point forward, the men and women did not hesitate to fight each other on either side.

This was a solid performance, but it definitely felt slow in places, and that prevented it from being as exciting as everything else we had seen on the show up until this. This was still a lot fun, but it lacked the level of energy you would have expected from an encounter of this nature until the last few minutes.

Marina was able to make Mone tap out to get the win for her team. The Cut attacked Moxley and Shafir after the match was over. The other Death Riders and members of The Conglomeration came out to join the fight.

Result: Shafir and Moxley defeated White and Mone

Having Mercedes officially join The Cut would be cool. The group might benefit from having her around.

The feud between White and Shafir should lead to the first real intergender singles match in AEW.

The Young Bucks and Jack Perry vs. Don Callis Family

Kevin Knight, Brian Cage and El Clon had a trios match this week against Jack Perry, Nick and Matt Jackson.

This match felt a bit random since none of these men are really feuding at the moment, but that didn't stop it from being entertaining. They might have relied too much on multi-man spots, but that is kind of how these bouts usually go in AEW.

The Bucks and Perry controlled the pace throughout most of the first half, but the DCF took control during the break.

Had this bout started the show, it probably would have felt much more exciting, but it came after so many other matches fans were looking forward to that it was almost impossible for them to live up to the first two hours.

The final couple of minutes were the most exciting stretch, which is usually the case with bouts like this. All six men brought something different to the table. When it was all over, the Bucks and Perry emerged as the winners.

Result: Perry and The Bucks beat The Don Callis Family

It was nice not having to hear Don on commentary so much this week.

Perry's arm drag from the top rope looked a little awkward but it was hard to say where it didn't line up.

Knight jumping over El Clon to hit a springboard clothesline was a cool spot.

Perry's poison rana on the floor was great.

Knight is so good at so many things. It feels like just a matter of time before he has a singles title again.

The way the Bucks launched Perry into Cage for a flying knee was awesome.

Wardlow was in singles action this week against ROH's Nick Comoroto. This was a pretty evenly matched showdown in terms of size and strength.

Even though this was not a complete squash, it still qualified because Wardlow won with ease in just a couple of minutes.

This wasn't bad for what it was, but it's hard to say it was good. It felt like filler on a show that needed no filler becasue it was already past the scheduled end of the show.

The Swirl vs. El Sky Team (ROH Tag Titles)

Mascara Dorada and Mistico put the ROH tag titles on the line against Lee Johnson and Blake Christian this week.

If you're familiar with these four men, then you know how this match played out without us even saying anything.

These are four talented guys who can all work at a fast pace while employing a lot of high-flying offense. It was going to be a fun match regardless of who came away with the win.

This was a well-structured bout that gave both teams several opportunities to impress the crowd.

Dorada and Mistico were able to pull off the win to retain the titles. It would have been cool to see a title change here, but the bout was enjoyable nonetheless.

Their celebration was cut short by Nick Wayne coming out to brag about beating Christ Jericho twice.

Vanilla Baby is still one of the weirdest nicknames for a wrestler.

The destroyer on the apron did not look good. Mistico barely made the rotation.

Queen Aminata vs. Skye Blue vs. Hyan (TBS Title)

The final match of the night saw Queen Aminata defend her TBS title against Skye Blue and Hyan.

Hayn took control right out of the gate and had both opponents in opposite corners. She was able to keep both of them at bay until the show went to a break.

The second half saw all three women get in plenty of offense on each other. All three of them took some nice bumps, but Aminata might have had the most painful moment when Blue threw a chair right at her face.

Despite being at a disadvantage, Aminata was able to get the win. Britt Baker showed up to taunt her after the match as a distraction so Persephone could attack her from behind. Maya World showed up to make the save at the end.

Result: Aminata defeated Blue and Persephone

The Coming to America reference in Aminata's entrance music is perfect.

Hyan has been around AEW for a while, but she has made a lot of noticeable improvements over the past year.

It was a little surprising that Thekla and Julia Hart were not at ringside, especially since we knew they were in the building after their promo earlier.

The way Aminata sold the chair Blue threw at her face was great.

The go-home episode of Dynamite and Collision before Full Gear this weekend did a good job hyping the PPV while also featuring some great action, but it may have been a little too bloated.

The show ended up going another 40 minutes past the end of the third hour, making this an almost four-hour broadcast.

The fact that this show had two squash matches felt unnecessary, and it slowed down the pace of the episode at times, but not enough to prevent it from being a strong show.

Ospreay and Fletcher had an outstanding promo segment to open the show, but FTR and MCMG stole the show with the final encounter in their Best of Five series.

Full Gear has a lot of matches with the potential to steal the show, but the world title bout with Ospreay and Fletcher is definitely the main focus.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi memoir: The 1966 fight between Muhammad Ali and Henry Cooper that former Congress president remembers from her Cambridge days
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Sonia and the '60s is also a tale of a young girl swept in the tide of civil rights blowing across the globe.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Sonia and the '60s is also a tale of a young girl swept in the tide of civil rights blowing across the globe.In her memoir 'Belonging', mentioning Martin Luther King, "free speech movement" in Berkeley and students movements in Europe as the influences on her generation, the Congress matriarch has fleetingly, but noticeably, referred to an indelible episode from the timeless story of boxing great Muhammad Ali. This was among the "memorable moments" in Cambridge after Sonia met Rajiv Gandhi. On a May 1966 evening, Sonia and friends gathered at a friend's place glued to the radio to listen to "the blow-by-blow boxing match between Ali and British boxer Henry Cooper."She adds, "when Clay beat Cooper in the sixth round of the match, we roared in triumph. It was for us not just a victory in a sport but a moral one as well. We had been roused by Martin Luther King Jr's massive demonstration in Washington and his 'I have a dream' speech."It was a momentous evening - not just for the prize fight - but for the times it represented. Two years ago, Ali had not only become the world heavyweight champion, acquired a reputation as a blabbermouth, but also a flaming rebel and a political lightening rod who shook the white establishment of Jim Crow America with his black pride assertion.A rebellion that would take him to oppose the draft to fight in the Vietnam War with that stinging barb - "I ain't got no quarrel with 'em VietCong". It led to his exile from boxing, before his return four years later shook the world more than his initial avatar, interspersed with gladiatorial battles like 'Rumble in the Jungle' and 'Thrilla in Manila'. But prior to Ali's exile were his two fights with Cooper, the British champion. The first was in 1963 as Cassius Clay, then still a braggard who backed his claims with heavy punches and floored opponents with blinding speed. Clay went to London in the hope of mopping up points to force the reigning heavyweight champion, the scary Sonny Liston to give him a chance at the title.This was the fight that is remembered for trainer Angelo Dundee's gamesmanship that saved the day for Clay and kept him in business for future. Who knows if it had turned out differently.Clay had mocked Cooper like he did to all - predicting to end it in five rounds. But 'Enry's 'Ammer', that dreaded left hook (hammer) that Cooper was famous for, put Clay on his backside in the fourth round. Ali later said, "it made me feel as if I had gone back and visited all my ancestors in Africa". It was enough, almost. But a small split in the seam of one glove, that trainer Angelo Dundee had seen before the fight but retained presciently for an emergency, was now put to good use .As Ali "slumped on his stool like a sack of potatoes", Dundee stuck his finger in the split and made it bigger and then asked the referee for a change of gloves. That earned Clay enough seconds to return to his senses. He recovered to batter Cooper. A year later, Clay shocked the world by defeating Liston twice, embraced Islam and became the most famous man on earth.As the heavyweight champion and a global icon, Clay returned to London as Ali for a 1966 rematch with Cooper. This was the phase when, along with protests, Malcolm X and King, Ali himself was the flush face of the fight for social justice.The bout itself, though, was an anticlimax. Unlike the heroic failure of the first fight, Cooper was no match this time. And the duel was stopped in the 6th round with Cooper bleeding profusely.And this was the outcome that Sonia and friends rejoiced over that evening, at a friend’s dig at Cambridge, as a “moral victory”.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Gavin Gwynne: The workaholic with a tattooed throat – meet The Merthyr Mexican
articles.summary: Welsh boxer Gavin Gwynne faces Zelfa Barrett at Wembley on 14 November as he aims for an unlikely world title shot.
articles.body:
It might be the giant sombrero that the rugged lightweight wears to the ring, in keeping with his moniker of 'The Merthyr Mexican'.

Or it will be the roaring lion prominently inked on his throat that invites the second glances and stares.

Lately, though, the proud valleys fighter is showing there are more reasons for people to take note.

Having already won British, Commonwealth and European titles, his upset of previously 16-fight unbeaten Khaleel Majid in May won him the WBA international belt at the weight above - and shot the 36-year-old up the rankings.

Now, as he prepares to face Manchester's Zelfa Barrett for the WBA intercontinental lightweight title at Wembley Arena on Saturday, 14 November, Gwynne knows he has a chance to be known for more than a nickname and a neck tattoo.

"I'm 36 but just feel like I'm getting better," Gwynne told BBC Sport Wales.

"Just look at Anthony Cacace, he was 35 when he won his world title. That's what I want. I want these big fights, even if I can get a title shot.

"All I have to do is win this fight and it pushes me in contention. It's must-win."

Facing Pacquiao in Cardiff would be honour for Cordina

Price rules out Shields but hints at big showdown

Gwynne believes it is possible too, having already achieved more than he thought he could when he swapped carpentry and building sites to go full-time just a few years ago.

Maybe it will redress a balance, Gwynne feeling he has not got the credit his 'fight all-comers' mantra has deserved.

Sharing a gym with one former world champion, Joe Cordina, and preparing for Barrett with tough sparring sessions up against another in Lee Selby, Gwynne suggests he has even been overlooked in his homeland.

"Maybe it's because I haven't got one of those eye-catching styles," he wondered aloud.

"But if you watch me, I'm always giving my all and for 12 rounds I'll give anyone nightmares."

The stories behind the nickname and the neck tattoo

There are a fair few fighters who will attest to that, with even his most recent defeat – in November 2024 to the undefeated Cameron Vuong – booed by the crowd who seemed to disagree with the judges' scorecards.

Most fights tend to be – for better or worse – a war with Gwynne, noted when he stepped into a Mexican gym in Los Angeles.

"That's where the nickname came from," he smiled.

"The coach came out [just] as me and this local guy were sparring lumps out of each other.

"He asked me where I was from and I told him 'Merthyr' as if he was going to know where that was, and he said: "Oh, the Merthyr Mexican!"

"It suits as I'm non-stop and I just love fighting. It's just in me."

So if that is the nickname, what about the tattoo? It turns out, that is also something Gwynne feels comes from within.

"That lion is inside me, always trying to get out, so that's what's behind it," Gwynne explained of the arresting ink work over his throat that took four hours to complete.

"The pain was unbearable to be honest. I had to stick it because I wouldn't have gone back to finish it if I'd left."

If the tattoo is hard to ignore, Gwynne is hardly the 'look-at-me' kind.

He is a fighter more of sweat and slog than show-off, even putting his recent rise down to Lockett holding him back from training so much and instructing him to take more time to rest.

"I was draining myself and I was leaving it all in the gym," said Gwynne. "Come fight night, I didn't have anything left."

Now, there could be more to come if Gwynne can overcome Barrett, knowing it could put him on the road to world level.

"It's a massive step - and, as I say, it's must win because I haven't got time to build myself back up now," he added, casting a glance at some of the young Welsh hopefuls in Lockett's gym.

For now, though, all eyes are on Gwynne.

articles.title: UFC: Usman Nurmagomedov slaps Merab Dvalishvili to spark mass brawl in Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov are involved in a physical altercation in Abu Dhabi.
articles.body:
Former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov were involved in a mass brawl in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday.

A video of the incident appeared to show Russian Nurmagomedov slap Dvalishvili after approaching the Georgian from behind.

Fighting then broke out between the two and members of their teams in a hotel lobby.

Dvalishvili, 35, is scheduled to compete at the Real American Freestyle (RAF) event in the United Arab Emirates on Saturday, against Brazilian Marlon Moraes.

Dvalishvili called Nurmagomedov, 28, and his team "snakes" in a video he later shared on TikTok as he received treatment on his bloodied face.

"What a sneaky way, guys," Dvalishvili said.

"What kind of fighters you guys are? What kind of man does this? If you want to try, let's do it the real way."

'Crazy' I'll get to 'knock my boss out' - Doumbe

UFC 334: Gane v Hokit - all you need to know

Dvalishvili called Nurmagomedov's older brother, Umar, "spoiled" before beating him in a bantamweight title fight in 2025.

Umar Nurmagomedov is due to take on American Urijah Faber at Saturday's event.

There was previously an altercation between the two camps before the RAF event in July.

UFC champion Islam Makhachev, who is a close friend and training partner of the Nurmagomedovs, suggested that incident led to Wednesday's altercation.

"Why were you silent when Merab hit a Dagestani wrestler for nothing and hurt his honor?" Makhachev wrote.

"Merab started what happened today in his homeland by allowing himself to hit a guest and insulting his mother."

Two-weight UFC champion Ilia Topuria, a friend of Dvalishvili, shared the footage of the incident on X and wrote: "Usman has reportedly been detained, along with the cowards who were with him.

"What a disgrace. A bunch of absolute cowards. I always thought you were a bunch of mediocre individuals. Now you've removed every last doubt.

"Honour, respect, and humility aren't words you preach. They're values you live by. And you've shown none of them."

Nurmagomedov is a free agent after his last fight with the PFL and has been heavily linked with a switch to the UFC.

MMA fighters often compete in RAF events alongside their careers in bigger promotions, with the likes of Khamzat Chimaev, Arman Tsarukyan and Colby Covington all recently appearing in the promotion.

articles.title: Alistair Overeem vs Jimi Manuwa added to Jake Paul's Christmas Eve fight card in Dubai
articles.summary: Alistair Overeem makes his professional boxing debut against Britain's Jimi Manuwa in a six-round heavyweight bout on the Christmas Eve card headlined by Jake Paul in Dubai; the YouTuber-turned boxer returns against Cedric Doumbe, 12 months on from having his jaw broken by Anthony Joshua
articles.body:
Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) have confirmed that Overeem, known as 'The Demolition Man', and 'Poster Boy' Manuwa will meet in a six-round professional heavyweight boxing bout on the undercard of Paul's cruiserweight clash with Cedric Doumbe in Dubai.

Former Strikeforce heavyweight champion and K-1 World Grand Prix winner Overeem said: "I've fought the best in the world, and I've been a world champion in multiple disciplines. Now I'm starting a new chapter in boxing, and I'm not here to make up the numbers.

"Jimi Manuwa is a dangerous man with serious knockout power, but I've built my career on taking the toughest challenges in combat sports"

Manuwa, who began his professional MMA career in 2008, won his first 14 professional fights before establishing himself among the UFC's most dangerous strikers.

He retired from MMA in 2019 with a 17-6 record, with 15 of his 17 victories coming by knockout or technical knockout. The 46-year-old returned to competition in August 2026, making a successful professional boxing debut with a second-round TKO victory over former UFC heavyweight Chase Sherman.

Manuwa said: "London is in everything I do. Where I come from, pressure makes you, and it makes me.

"I've watched Alistair since I was coming up, and I know exactly what he's capable of. That's why I wanted this fight.

"After my win in Orlando, I wasn't looking for an easy opponent. On Christmas Eve, one of us is going to sleep, and it's not going to be me."

Overeem vs Manuwa adds another explosive encounter to the card headlined by global superstar Paul, on his return to the ring a year on from suffering a broken jaw in a sixth-round stoppage loss to former two-time unified heavyweight world champion Anthony Joshua.

MVP chief executive Nakisa Bidarian said: "Netherlands' Alistair Overeem and the United Kingdom's Jimi Manuwa are two of the most recognisable names in combat sports, with decades of experience competing against the best in the world and a combined 40 knockouts in MMA.

"Bringing these two legends together in a professional boxing match adds another compelling matchup to an already massive Christmas Eve event.

"With Jake Paul facing Cedric Doumbe in the main event, we're assembling a card that brings together some of the biggest personalities and most dangerous strikers in combat sports for fans in Dubai and around the world."

articles.title: Boxing: Briton Josh Kelly to face Jaron Ennis in February unification bout
articles.summary: Unbeaten two-weight world champion Jaron Ennis will look to end Josh Kelly's nine-fight winning streak.
articles.body:
Britain's Josh Kelly will fight Jaron Ennis in a light-middleweight unification bout on 27 February in Atlanta.

Kelly, 32, holds the IBF world title and challenges American Ennis for the WBA and WBO belts.

Ennis is unbeaten in 37 fights with one no-contest, while Sunderland's Kelly is on a nine-fight winning streak that includes him capturing his maiden world title in January.

Kelly will be the underdog against 29-year-old Ennis, who became a two-weight world champion when he beat Xander Zayas in June.

"I've waited a very long time to prove myself at the highest level, finally I have that moment," said Kelly.

Kelly represented Team GB at the 2016 Olympics, but his professional career was derailed by a loss to David Avanesyan in 2021.

The Englishman slowly rebuilt and recovered from being knocked down to beat Russian Bakhram Murtazaliev in their world title fight at the start of the year.

He then outpointed Northern Irishman Caoimhin Agyarko in his first defence in July.

The winner of Ennis v Kelly will hold three world titles, with Sebastian Fundora holding the WBC belt.

Eddie Hearn promotes both fighters and says the victor will "lay the foundations to a legacy in the sport".

There has not been an undisputed champion at light-middleweight since Jermell Charlo achieved the feat in 2022.

"Boots and Josh are both brilliant world champions and this was not a difficult fight to make when you lay out what is there for the winner – three belts around your waist and just one more to collect to become undisputed," added Hearn.

articles.title: B/R Staff Predictions for UFC 334 Main Card
articles.summary: It's that time of year again.
articles.body:
This Saturday, the UFC will make its annual November stop in New York City, and there is a ton of high-quality MMA to look forward to.

In the main event, Ciryl Gane will attempt to defend the heavyweight title against trash-talking challenger Josh Hokit. It's a very interesting style clash on paper, and it should bring some order to the heavyweight division, which has been in shambles for years, most recently because Tom Aspinall was forced to abdicate the throne after suffering career-threatening eye injuries in a fight with Gane.

There will also be gold up for grabs in the co-main event, as women's bantamweight champ Kayla Harrison takes on the returning Amanda Nunes, who is almost inarguably the best female fighter in MMA history.

Earlier on the card, we'll get an interesting middleweight matchup between Caio Borralho and Yousri Belgaroui, and a high-stakes welterweight scrap between entertaining gatekeeper Kevin Holland and red-hot contender Uros Medić. The main card opener, meanwhile, will see Bilal Hasan attempt to take another step up the flyweight rankings against Luis Gurule.

Here's how the B/R combat sports squad sees it all going down inside Madison Square Garden.

Heavyweight Title: Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit

Nick Akerman: Josh Hokit is obviously a very dangerous fighter, but his express run to a UFC heavyweight title shot will be thoroughly examined when he gets into the Octagon with Ciryl Gane.

Hokit's win over Curtis Blaydes was impressive; those guys absolutely went for it, but I don't think beating Derrick Lewis, Denzel Freeman, and Max Gimenis is enough to put him in this position. Blaydes is nowhere near Gane's level.

The Frenchman is massive, a scary striker, and an all-round better athlete than Hokit. He looked great against Tom Aspinall before the eye poke, then walked through Alex Pereira. I think he's going to break Hokit down across multiple rounds and put him through hell before getting a highlight win against a fighter who probably needs to be taken down a peg or two.

Tom Taylor: This is a bit of a tough fight to call, mainly because I'm still not totally sold on Gane, even after his recent knockout of Alex Pereira. I just can't erase the memory of him getting absolutely wiped out by Jon Jones a few years back.

That said, I'm even less sold on Hokit, who has looked good against two veteran contenders, Curtis Blaydes and Derrick Lewis, but has more or less talked his way into this title opportunity.

For that reason, I've got to side with Gane in this one. Hokit's wrestling and pace could make things interesting, but I think the champ is clever enough to break his challenger down over a few rounds and ultimately finish him. One variable to keep an eye on is whether he loses points for the fouls he lands in nearly every fight—refs finally seem to be cracking down on this stuff—but I don't see that being a huge factor, especially if he gets a finish.

Adam Kramer: Can Hokit take Gane to the ground? And if so, how fast? This fascinating fight isn't that easy to assess, but it feels that way in many respects.

For all of Hokit's antics and theatrics, his fighting style is straightforward and really difficult to deal with at the heavyweight level. His elite wrestling skills have been on display since he made a name for himself on the Contender Series.

But his gas tank, in many respects, is the coal that powers the engine. It's not just the way he takes opponents down; it's his ability to relentlessly overwhelm opponents. And the fact that he was able to power through his fight against Curtis Blaydes despite taking and giving so many shots is eye-opening.

Yes, Gane will make things tough. He's bigger, taller, and has an enormous reach advantage. He's also a very tactical fighter despite his size, something we saw against both Tom Aspinall and Alex Pereira.

He is more dangerous and more powerful. Simple as that. And if he connects against Hokit, look out. But the wrestling, pressure, and gas tank are enormous variables, especially if and when we get to later rounds.

Hokit finds a way to win, and the microphone work that follows will unquestionably be off the rails.

Prediction: Hokit by unanimous decision.

Women's Bantamweight Title: Kayla Harrison vs. Amanda Nunes

Nick Akerman: Gah, this is one of those fights that we've probably waited too long for. Amanda Nunes is three years into retirement. Kayla Harrison is 10 months post-neck surgery. It's an incredibly hard bout to call, even if I think Nunes would have walked it back in her prime.

Harrison has never been hit by someone with Nunes' power. I think she's capable of taking Nunes down and establishing control—that strength isn't to be underestimated—but I'm not sure she's got enough to get a finish.

It's always incredibly difficult to know what a returning fighter will look like, but a motivated Nunes is still as dangerous as anyone out there and should have enough to overcome an excellent opponent.

Prediction: Nunes by unanimous decision.

Tom Taylor: This is another really tough fight to call, simply because there are so many variables at play. As Nick said, Harrison is returning from a difficult surgery, and Nunes is returning from a three-year retirement. Because of that, it's really difficult to say how either woman will look in the Octagon.

Still, I'm going to go with Nunes. The simplest explanation is that she is the best female fighter in MMA history—far greater than Harrison, who is phenomenal in her own right.

However, I'm also thinking about Harrison's lone MMA loss to Larissa Pacheco, who is kind of a less refined, less versatile version of Nunes.

If Nunes is anywhere near top form, she should be able to win this one. She'll probably have to get back to her feet a few times, but eventually, she'll start landing with consequence, and the finish won't be far off from there.

Adam Kramer: There are some unique elements to consider in this fight, and we won't know exactly how each plays out until sometime late Saturday evening. Harrison is coming off surgery that sidelined her for an extended period; Nunes is coming back after years away from the sport.

The oddsmakers believe Harrison will have the easier transition back, and perhaps that makes sense. Still, she hasn't fought since June 2025, which is to say she's not exactly coming into this one in form, either.

Despite the extended time away, Nunes is still the greatest female force in MMA history. While she will undoubtedly have to deal with Harrison's takedown attempts, she'll also present the toughest challenge Harrison has ever faced.

Again, lots of questions. If in doubt, however, we go with the GOAT.

Prediction: Nunes by unanimous decision .

Middleweight: Caio Borralho vs. Yousri Belgaroui

Nick Akerman: It's skill check time for Yousri Belgaroui.

The giant kickboxer heads into this one on a heater, with four straight knockouts against lowly opposition. Caio Borralho is a step up in competition; he's well-rounded, has overcome a decent range of foes, and has the speed and power combination to put Belgaroui in danger.

Although Belgaroui is likely the underdog, his skill set could expose Borralho a little bit. The Brazilian sometimes appears to second-guess himself when he should press on, relying on single shots, which may leave an opening for Belgaroui to do what he does best. I think there's a potential shock waiting for us.

Tom Taylor: It's been fun watching Yousri Belgaroui get established in the UFC middleweight division, but this seems like a gargantuan step up for him.

While he's clearly more technical than Caio Borralho in the striking department, he will be sharing the cage with a fighter who boasts plenty of firepower and, more importantly, a great grappling game.

So long as Borralho keeps his ego in check and relies on his clear grappling advantage, I see no reason why he can't win this one comfortably over three rounds.

Prediction: Borralho by unanimous decision.

Adam Kramer: While the main and co-main are supremely enticing, don't sleep on this one. Neither fighter has lost more than three fights, and Belgaroui has ended his last four fights early.

Belgaroui, of course, will put his kickboxing prowess to the test against a huge leap up in competition. As such, expect Borralho to try to make this fight ugly. He would be wise to clinch or even bring this fight to the mat if he can.

Getting to that point, of course, won't be easy. Belgaroui will have a substantial height and reach advantage, which should serve him well here.

While the grappling is worrying—as is Borralho's seasoning—this will be a test for both fighters. And although Belgaroui is about to be tested in a way he hasn't before, we wouldn't be shocked if he passes it emphatically.

Welterweight: Uros Medić vs. Kevin Holland

Nick Akerman: I'm as surprised as the next person that Uros Medić is sitting on a four-fight winning streak in the UFC, all by knockout. He has proven devastating in the pocket recently, so Kevin Holland should make for an interesting matchup.

Holland can't afford to head into the Octagon with the slightly lazy, slightly languid style we've often seen from him. Medić is likely to push the pace and close the distance as quickly as possible.

As we saw against Geoff Neal, he barely needs an opening to launch one shot that will end the fight. Holland will know point-scoring might be too dangerous, and I can see him taking it to the ground to squeeze out control.

Prediction: Holland by unanimous decision.

Tom Taylor: This is such a weird matchup. After four straight KO wins, Medić obviously deserves somebody higher-ranked than Holland, who has been extremely inconsistent in the Octagon. At the same time, I don't think he will pass this test.

Holland has everything he needs to mount the upset in this matchup. He's got the range to keep himself away from Medić's surprising power, the chin to withstand the shots he can't avoid, and most importantly, an underrated grappling game that will help him dictate where the fight occurs.

I'm not discounting another Medić KO—he's been proving me wrong a lot lately—but I think his run ends here. Holland gets him down and eventually locks up a submission.

Prediction: Holland by submission. Rd. 2.

Adam Kramer: The more dangerous fighter of late has been Medić, who has finished four opponents since January of 2025. His most recent fight against Daniel Rodriguez lasted a grand total of 30 seconds, and his last four wins have taken less than four minutes overall.

It's impressive, to say the least. It also might be a bit worrisome. He hasn't seen a second round since November of 2023. Needless to say, it's been a minute.

Holland has largely been a magician at avoiding big shots, and his staggering 10-inch reach advantage should pay huge dividends. I would also expect we see plenty of clinching and maybe even takedowns from Holland, who has built such a robust arsenal of skills for fights like these.

Holland should threaten a submission or two (or more) and keep Medić on his toes.

Flyweight Bout: Bilal Hasan vs. Luis Gurule

Nick Akerman: Bilal Hasan is going to be an extremely entertaining addition to the UFC, whichever way his fights go.

He was super loose in his win against Nilson Rojas, where he handed out punishment while taking a lot back before landing a beautiful second-round knockout. I'm not sure Luis Gurule will push him as much.

Hasan is the taller man, possesses a huge reach advantage, and should be able to get a similar result against an opponent who has one win in five since receiving the call-up from Dana White's Contender Series.

Tom Taylor: The UFC clearly sees some star potential in Bilal Hasan, which explains why they have given him such a winnable matchup in the main card opener of such a huge event. He's being set up to extend his highlight reel and continue his march toward the top of the flyweight division, which is arguably better than it's ever been before.

We've seen guys in Hasan's spot come up short before, but this really does feel like a layup for him. He's going to have a lot of physical advantages, he's clearly the harder hitter, and his opponent has made a habit of losing in the Octagon.

Hasan stays unbeaten with another slick stoppage on the feet.

Adam Kramer: While most of the fights on the card feature tight fight odds and underdog potential, this doesn't feel like one of those fights.

Hasan is being fast-tracked by the UFC, which explains why such an enormous favorite is opening up the main card. He's 10-0, and nine of those wins have come by finish. He's still just 25 years old, although a lack of experience shouldn't slow him down.

Gurule, meanwhile, has lost four of his last five fights. He's smaller, has a significant reach disadvantage, and is severely outclassed. Perhaps his experience helps, although it just doesn't feel that way.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi Police confirm 10 arrests after Nurmagomedov-Dvalishvili hotel brawl, including two who filmed viral footage
articles.summary: Abu Dhabi Police have arrested 10 individuals following a hotel brawl involving UFC fighters Usman Nurmagomedov and Merab Dvalishvili, raising concerns for their upcoming fight participation and legal implications.
articles.body: Abu Dhabi Police have confirmed the arrest of 10 people following a high-profile brawl involving Usman Nurmagomedov, former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and members of their respective camps. The confrontation erupted in a hotel lobby on Thursday, just two days before Real American Freestyle (RAF) stages its first-ever event in Abu Dhabi and its Middle East debut on November 14. The arrests have raised questions over the fighters' participation in the historic card and the potential legal consequences for those involved.Usman Nurmagomedov approaches Dvalishvili during hotel interviewThe incident took place on Thursday, November 11, at the Yas Hilton hotel in Abu Dhabi, where former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili was giving an interview ahead of his appearance at RAF Abu Dhabi. The Georgian was speaking with Saba Lazishvili in the hotel lobby when Usman Nurmagomedov approached with members of his entourage.Footage shared widely on social media shows Nurmagomedov walking towards Dvalishvili from behind before exchanging words with him and slapping him across the face. A fight then broke out between the two groups, with Nurmagomedov and his associates on one side and Dvalishvili and Lazishvili on the other.Dvalishvili later posted videos showing his bloodied face and receiving medical treatment for a cut. He alleged that he and his younger friend had been attacked by a much larger group, and said hotel security had prevented him from responding while the other group continued the assault.“Was doing an interview for RAF in hotel lobby and Usman and his buddies came up from behind and started punching me and my young friend,” Dvalishvili wrote in a social media caption. “Security was holding me - they kept kicking us when we were down like losers.”The Georgian also described the confrontation as a “sneaky” attack, claiming that he and a friend had faced approximately 20 people. The footage and his posts showed the aftermath, including the injuries to his face.Abu Dhabi Police confirm arrestsAbu Dhabi Police confirmed on Thursday evening that 10 people had been arrested in connection with the incident. Eight were identified as individuals involved in the fight, while two others were arrested for filming it. All were referred to the Public Prosecution for further legal proceedings.In its official statement, the force said:“The Abu Dhabi General Police were able to arrest 8 individuals involved in a fight that occurred at the entrance of one of the hotels, following previous disputes between them. They also managed to arrest two individuals who filmed the incident and took the necessary legal action against them, referring them to the Public Prosecution to complete the procedures in accordance with the applicable laws.The details of the incident revolve around a fight that occurred at the entrance of one of the hotels, following previous disputes between several individuals. Immediately, the specialized teams in Abu Dhabi Police began their procedures to deal with the incident, and were able to arrest those involved, in addition to arresting the two individuals who filmed the fight, and taking the necessary legal action against them.The Abu Dhabi Police emphasized their commitment to maintaining security and public order, and dealing firmly with behaviors that may disrupt security or endanger the safety of others, stressing the importance of adhering to laws and regulations and adopting civilized and responsible behavior.”The National reported that Dvalishvili was not the person pressing charges, with police alerted because the incident occurred in public and was captured on camera. Authorities confirmed the arrests but had not identified those detained at the time of writing, leaving it unclear whether Usman Nurmagomedov, Umar Nurmagomedov or Merab Dvalishvili were among those arrested.The arrests followed reports that Nurmagomedov and members of his group had been detained and questioned. MMA journalist Ariel Helwani wrote on X: “As of this writing, everyone involved in the hotel brawl is still being detained by the local authorities, I’m told.”UFC fighter Ilia Topuria, a close friend of Dvalishvili, also claimed that Nurmagomedov had been detained, posting: “has reportedly been detained, along with the cowards who were with him.”“I always thought you were a bunch of mediocre individuals. Now you’ve removed every last doubt. Honor, respect, and humility aren’t words you preach. They’re values you live by. And you’ve shown none of them.”Why the two camps have a history of hostilityThe confrontation was not an isolated disagreement between fighters meeting in a hotel. It followed a series of disputes involving Dvalishvili and members of the Nurmagomedov camp, with tensions dating back to their UFC rivalry in January 2025.Dvalishvili defeated Umar Nurmagomedov, Usman's older brother, by unanimous decision at UFC 311 on January 18, 2025, retaining his bantamweight championship. It was the first successful defence of his title and the first professional defeat of Umar's career. The contest was also named Fight of the Night.The hostility had developed before they entered the octagon. Dvalishvili publicly called Umar “spoiled” and accused him of disrespect, remarks that contributed to an increasingly bitter exchange between the two camps. The rivalry did not end with the Georgian's victory, and subsequent encounters outside the UFC intensified the personal nature of the dispute.Tensions resurfaced at a Real American Freestyle event in Georgia later in July 2025. Dvalishvili was involved in a backstage altercation with an associate of Umar's, during which he slapped one of the Dagestani fighter's friends. The incident prompted further exchanges between the camps.UFC lightweight champion Islam Makhachev later claimed that the confrontation was retaliation for Dvalishvili striking a Dagestani wrestler and insulting his mother.The Abu Dhabi incident now brings Usman Nurmagomedov directly into the confrontation. Unlike Umar, he has not fought Dvalishvili in the UFC, but his involvement in the hotel altercation has drawn attention because of his relationship with the former bantamweight champion's previous opponent and the history between their respective groups.Why Usman Nurmagomedov was in Abu DhabiNurmagomedov, 28, was in Abu Dhabi to support his older brother Umar, rather than compete on the RAF card. Umar is scheduled to face former UFC champion Urijah Faber on Saturday, November 14, at the Etihad Arena, as part of the organisation's first event in the Middle East.Dvalishvili is also scheduled to compete on the card, facing Marlon Moraes in a catchweight crossover match.The 28-year-old Russian is one of the most prominent lightweight fighters outside the UFC and is currently a free agent after completing his contract with the Professional Fighters League. He has won 22 of his 23 professional contests, with the remaining bout recorded as a no contest.Nurmagomedov previously won and defended the Bellator lightweight championship twice before capturing the vacant PFL lightweight title in a rematch against Paul Hughes. He subsequently stopped Alfie Davis and Archie Colgan in title defences, with his most recent appearance producing a first-round knockout of Colgan in July.His contract situation had already made him one of the most closely watched names in the sport. Nurmagomedov reportedly turned down a $2 million offer to re-sign with the PFL, and the organisation's 90-day exclusive negotiating period expired on October 29. He is consequently expected to attract interest from the UFC as he considers his next move.UFC president Dana White acknowledged the organisation's interest when asked about the possibility of signing him last month. “We're interested,” White told The National.The hotel incident now comes at a sensitive point in Nurmagomedov's career, with his free-agent status and potential move to the UFC already attracting attention. His participation in the altercation, and the police action that followed, could become another factor surrounding his next professional move.RAF faces questions ahead of Saturday's eventThe timing of the brawl could hardly be worse for RAF, which is preparing to stage its first event in Abu Dhabi and its Middle East debut on November 14. Dvalishvili is scheduled to face Marlon Moraes, while Umar Nurmagomedov is set to wrestle Urijah Faber. However, the arrests and ongoing police proceedings have left the availability of the two fighters an immediate concern ahead of Saturday's card.The RAF is expected to address the incident at Thursday's pre-event press conference, with its officials set to provide the organisation's response ahead of Saturday's card. The event marks the promotion's first in the Middle East, with Dvalishvili and Umar Nurmagomedov both scheduled to compete. It remains unclear whether the confrontation or subsequent police proceedings will affect their participation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: UFC 334: Kayla Harrison on verge of 'permanent nerve damage' before neck surgery
articles.summary: Kayla Harrison says she was "on the verge of having permanent nerve damage" before having neck and spinal surgery at the start of the year.
articles.body:
Kayla Harrison says she was "on the verge of having permanent nerve damage" before undergoing neck and spinal surgery at the start of the year.

The American was set to defend her UFC women's bantamweight world title against Amanda Nunes in January but the fight was postponed when Harrison discovered she required an operation.

Harrison, a two-time Olympic judo gold medallist, had surgery on five herniated discs in her neck accumulated following a lifetime in combat sports.

The 36-year-old says the recovery from surgery left her questioning her future in the sport, but after some "soul searching" she decided to return.

Harrison will now defend her belt against returning Brazilian hall-of-famer Nunes at UFC 334 in New York on Saturday.

"Physically, I was preparing for the biggest fight of my life, and I was obviously having an immense amount of pain, having lightning bolts," said Harrison.

"I was on the verge of having permanent nerve damage, but I was also training as if I wasn't. So, I was in the best shape of my life, as good of shape as I could be with that - and then I was in a neck brace for eight weeks.

"I did not feel like myself. I did not feel good - I did not feel good in my body."

The bout with Nunes is being billed as one of the biggest women's MMA fights of all time.

The pair are friends and were team-mates at American Top Team Gym before Nunes left in 2022.

Nunes, 38, is widely regarded as one of the greatest MMA fighters of all time and is returning to the sport after retiring in 2023.

She is a former featherweight and bantamweight champion and the only woman in history to hold two UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously.

Harrison is a two-time former PFL champion before claiming UFC gold in only her third fight in the promotion last year.

She says the prospect of competing against Nunes was a driving factor behind her successful recovery.

"Mentally, to go from that high and that low is hard, and when I was finally able to get back on the mat, I really struggled with confidence," said Harrison.

"I think I was so scared to hurt my neck again, number one. That lack of confidence made me question if I was ever gonna feel like me again.

"So, I had a lot of soul-searching to do. If I was just being a mum, I could be fine. But getting back to the Kayla that I was, was really hard. It's been hard, but it's been worth it."

Harrison has won 19 of her 20 fights since her MMA debut in 2018, with her only defeat coming against Larissa Pacheco in 2022.

After questioning her future in the sport over the past 12 months, Harrison did not confirm if the fight with Nunes would be her last.

"We'll cross that bridge when we get to it," added Harrison.

"We'll see. I'm really grateful to be back doing what I love again against the greatest of all time, and I can't wait."

articles.title: India's Ambekar Meetei scripts history with boxing gold at Dakar Youth Olympics
articles.summary: India's Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei scripted history at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, striking gold in the men's 50kg boxing event after edging past
articles.body: India's Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei scripted history at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, striking gold in the men's 50kg boxing event after edging past Ireland's Kristian Jubani in a closely fought final.The Indian boxer secured a 3-2 victory on the judges' scorecards to claim the top prize. In a tightly contested bout, three judges favoured Ambekar Meetei, while the remaining two awarded their verdict to his Irish opponent.The gold medal capped an impressive campaign for the Manipuri boxer, who had earlier booked his place in the final with a commanding performance in the semifinals.Ambekar Meetei defeated Colombia's Izzon Jeffrey Galea Arevalo 5-0 to secure a unanimous points victory and move into the gold medal bout. His semifinal triumph was particularly significant as it ended India's 16-year wait for a boxer to reach the final of the Youth Olympics.The milestone matched the achievement of Shiva Thapa, who had made it to the final at the inaugural Youth Olympic Games in Singapore in 2010.Ambekar Meetei went a step further by converting his final appearance into a gold medal, giving India a historic triumph in the men's 50kg category.Hailing from Manipur, the young boxer trains at the National Institute of Sports (NIS) in Patiala. His gold medal in Dakar marks a memorable achievement for Indian boxing at the Youth Olympic Games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Kvaratskhelia apoya a Merab tras el ataque recibido: "Muestra al mundo lo que significa ser georgiano, hombre y ser humano"
articles.standfirst: El extremo del PSG se ha solidarizado con su compatriota
articles.summary: El extremo del PSG se ha solidarizado con su compatriota
articles.body: Tras el ataque por la espalda sufrido en Abu Dhabi ayer, un episodio viral que ha trascendido el mundo de las MMA y los deportes de contacto, numerosos deportistas y personalidades se han solidarizado con el ex campeón de la UFC Merab Dvalishvili. Entre ellos, un compatriota suyo, el georgiano Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, estrella en el PSG y bicampeón de la Champions las dos últimas temporadas. Kvaratskhelia compartió en su Instagram una imagen de la agresión de Usman Nurmagomedov y su equipo sobre Merab y Saba, junto con un mensaje en georgiano. “¡Merab, Saba! ¡Gracias y estamos con vosotros!. Muéstrenle al mundo una vez más lo que significa ser georgiano, hombre y ser humano. A diferencia de aquellos que, cobardemente, atacando por la espalda y de forma desigual, intentan oprimiros; los hombres no se comportan así y, por supuesto, no lo han conseguido ni lo conseguirán jamás con los georgianos”, escribía Kvaratskhelia. Mientras, tanto Merab como Saba Lazishvili, al igual que Usman Nurmagomedov y el resto de daguestaníes que participarón en la emboscada, siguen bajo custodia policial en Abu Dhabi. Así lo ha informado Zviad Lazishvili, hermano de Saba, y también el periodista Ariel Helwani.

articles.title: Paddy Pimblett vuelve a atacar a Ilia Topuria: "He oído que todo el mundo en España se ha vuelto en su contra"
articles.standfirst: El inglés habló en el podcast de Joe Rogan
articles.summary: El inglés habló en el podcast de Joe Rogan
articles.body: Como era de esperar, la aparición de Paddy Pimblett (24-4) en el podcast de Joe Rogan, uno de los más escuchados en habla inglesa, ha dejado ataques contra Ilia Topuria (17-1). El peleador 'scouser', gran rival del 'Matador' desde hace años, sigue en ascenso en el peso ligero y un combate en 2027 entre ambos... no es descartable. Sobre todo cuando el propio Topuria pidió el duelo recientemente. "¿Paddy? Me lo comería como la gran salchicha que es", había declarado días atrás Topuria en 'ABC'. Y ahora, claro, Paddy ha contestado al hispanogeorgiano. "¿Es georgiano, español o alemán? Elige uno, chico, no puedes ser las tres cosas a la vez. Deja de intentar conseguir seguidores de tres países diferentes. De todas formas, he oído que todo el mundo en España se ha vuelto en su contra. Ya había algunos rumores antes de que perdiera contra Justin, pero está claro que la cosa ha empeorado desde que perdió contra él. Será duro si lucho contra él y vuelve a perder; entonces no le quedará ni un solo seguidor", eran las palabras del de Liverpool en el programa de Joe Rogan. Unas declaraciones que buscan 'picar' a Ilia Topuria, más allá de ser verídicas o no las afirmaciones que hace, y volver a encender una rivalidad que desemboque en el esperadísimo combate entre ambos. De momento, mientras, está por ver qué depara el futuro a ambos peleadores. Paddy viene de ganar (el pasado mes de julio) a Benoit Saint-Denis con una espectacular sumisión antes del primer minuto de combate; Ilia, que sigue de baja tras UFC Casa Blanca, ya ha declarado que apunta al mes de abril de 2027.

articles.title: Abu Dhabi hotel brawl: Usman Nurmagomedov and co. could face up to one year in prison and AED 20,000 fine under UAE law after police arrest 10
articles.summary: Ten arrests made after a hotel brawl involving UFC fighters in Abu Dhabi. Potential penalties include up to one year in prison and fines under UAE law. Authorities act firmly against public safety threats.
articles.body: Ten people have been arrested following the hotel brawl involving members of the camps of Merab Dvalishvili and Usman Nurmagomedov, with Abu Dhabi Police referring those detained to the Public Prosecution. The authorities have yet to identify any of them, but the arrests raise questions about the potential penalties under UAE law, including possible prison sentences and fines for those found guilty.Abu Dhabi Police confirm 10 arrests after hotel brawlThe confrontation took place in the lobby of the Yas Hilton hotel on Wednesday, November 11, when former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili was conducting an interview ahead of his appearance at Real American Freestyle's (RAF) Abu Dhabi event. Usman Nurmagomedov approached with members of his entourage, and an exchange between the two groups escalated into a fight.Dvalishvili later shared footage showing a cut to his face and alleged that Nurmagomedov and his associates had attacked him and his friend. The incident came two days before RAF stages its first event in the Middle East, with Dvalishvili scheduled to face Marlon Moraes and Umar Nurmagomedov set to meet Urijah Faber on Saturday, November 14.Abu Dhabi Police confirmed on Thursday evening that 10 people had been arrested. Eight were identified as individuals involved in the fight, while two others were arrested for filming the incident. All 10 were referred to the Public Prosecution for further legal proceedings.In its statement, the police said the fight followed previous disputes between several individuals and stressed its commitment to maintaining public order and dealing firmly with behaviour that threatens public safety.However, the announcement did not identify any of those arrested. There has been no official confirmation that Usman Nurmagomedov, Umar Nurmagomedov or Dvalishvili is among the 10 people detained. Although reports have suggested that Usman was taken into custody, the police statement itself names none of the fighters, and their individual status remains unconfirmed.What prison sentence could those involved face?The potential punishment for physical assault depends largely on the injuries sustained and their consequences under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 31 of 2021, the country's Penal Code.Under Article 390, an assault that results in injuries causing incapacity for 20 days or less can carry a prison sentence of up to one year and a fine of up to AED 10,000 (approx. $2,700). That is the potential maximum penalty for the category of assault described in the legal provisions, not an automatic sentence for everyone involved in the hotel fight.More serious injuries can lead to heavier punishment. Where an assault leaves a victim unable to work for more than 20 days, the law provides for imprisonment and a fine, with the precise penalty depending on the circumstances and extent of the injury.The medical assessment of those involved could therefore become important in determining how prosecutors classify the incident. Dvalishvili shared footage of a facial cut and receiving treatment, but that alone does not establish the legal severity of his injuries. The authorities would need to consider medical evidence alongside the circumstances of the confrontation.The consequences could be more severe if prosecutors establish aggravating circumstances, including a premeditated attack or the involvement of multiple assailants. The footage circulated online shows several people involved in the confrontation, but it does not, by itself, establish who initiated the violence or the individual conduct of each person. Those findings would have to come through the investigation and legal proceedings.Could they also face public-order charges?The consequences may extend beyond physical assault. Under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 31 of 2021, conduct that disrupts public order or threatens public safety can attract additional criminal penalties.Under Article 210, participating in a gathering of at least five people in a public place under circumstances that threaten public security can carry imprisonment and a fine. If participants refuse to disperse after an order from the authorities, the legal consequences can become more serious. Where a gathering results in a disturbance of public peace or endangers others, the law provides for further penalties.Separately, Article 411 covers certain acts that violate public decency. Such offences can carry imprisonment of up to one year or a fine, depending on the conduct involved.Public insults and abusive language can also attract separate penalties under UAE law, with some offences carrying imprisonment of up to one year and fines of up to AED 20,000 (approx. $5,400).However, these are potential legal provisions, not automatic charges. Prosecutors would need to establish the specific conduct of each individual and whether the legal requirements for each offence were met.Could those who filmed the fight face separate penalties?The two arrests involving people who filmed the confrontation raise a separate legal issue. Abu Dhabi Police explicitly distinguished them from the eight people arrested for participating in the fight, confirming that they too had been referred to the Public Prosecution.UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 34 of 2021, which deals with cybercrime, includes provisions concerning privacy and the unauthorised recording or sharing of images and videos. Depending on the circumstances, the recording or circulation of footage without consent could attract separate legal scrutiny. However, the fact that two people were arrested for filming the incident does not establish which specific offence they may face or what punishment prosecutors might seek.What happens after the arrests?The referral of the 10 individuals to the Public Prosecution marks the next stage of the process. Prosecutors will examine the circumstances of the fight, the available footage, medical evidence and the conduct of those involved before determining what charges, if any, should follow.The fact that Dvalishvili reportedly did not intend to press charges does not, by itself, establish that the case will end. Police have already confirmed that they intervened following a public altercation and arrested those they identified as being involved, alongside the two people accused of filming it.For now, the central distinction remains between the confirmed arrests and the identities of those detained. Abu Dhabi Police have named no individuals, and there is no official confirmation that Dvalishvili, Usman Nurmagomedov or Umar Nurmagomedov is among them. Until the authorities identify the people involved and the Public Prosecution establishes the nature of any charges, the possible prison terms and fines remain dependent on the findings of the investigation.Could the Abu Dhabi incident derail Usman Nurmagomedov’s UFC ambitions?Usman Nurmagomedov’s anticipated move to the UFC could face complications as the Abu Dhabi investigation develops. The 28-year-old has established himself as one of the leading lightweights outside the promotion, and UFC president Dana White acknowledged the organisation’s interest last month, telling The National: “We're interested.” Nurmagomedov is now a free agent after his PFL contract expired and the organisation’s 90-day exclusive negotiating period ended on October 29.However, his conduct outside competition has previously attracted attention. At UFC 302 in June 2024, he entered the octagon to celebrate Islam Makhachev’s submission victory over Dustin Poirier before security escorted him away. He repeated the move in August after his brother Umar was knocked out by Song Yadong.The Abu Dhabi incident presents a more serious concern because it has resulted in arrests and a referral to the Public Prosecution. If Nurmagomedov faces criminal charges or a conviction, the outcome could influence the UFC’s assessment of a potential signing. There is no indication that the promotion has imposed a ban or taken disciplinary action against him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ilia Topuria: "Justin Gaethje no es nadie"
articles.standfirst: El peleador hispanogeorgiano ha vuelto a atacar a su verdugo en el UFC Casa Blanca tras sus negativas a realizar una revancha
articles.summary: El peleador hispanogeorgiano ha vuelto a atacar a su verdugo en el UFC Casa Blanca tras sus negativas a realizar una revancha
articles.body: Desde el pasado 14 de junio, hay pocas noticias acerca del futuro de Justin Gaethje. Aquel día, el peleador estadounidense cumplió el sueño de toda una vida tras finalizar a Ilia Topuria y convertirse en campeón indiscutido de peso ligero en el UFC Casa Blanca, y desde entonces no ha dejado muy claro cuál quiere que sea su siguiente paso. 'The Highlight' ha dejado caer la opción de la retirada, un posible regreso ante Arman Tsarukyan y ha mostrado su negativa a realizar una revancha contra 'El Matador', lo que ha provocado que Ilia le vuelva a atacar en una reciente entrevista con ABC. Topuria ha reconocido que lo que más le gustaría hacer a corto plazo es esa revancha para recuperar su cinturón y vengar su única derrota profesional, pero también ha afirmado que "Justin no es nadie. Imagínate: si yo peleo contra Paddy Pimblett, incluso siendo él campeón, tendría que ser la pelea co estelar". De hecho, ese combate contra 'The Baddy' es el que más opciones tiene de suceder, ya que sería el más mediático para la UFC y les permitiría incluso realizar un evento numerado sin la necesidad de que haya un cinturón de por medio. La rivalidad que mantienen Pimblett y Topuria ya es suficiente para llevar a cabo una de las carteleras más vendibles de la historia, de ahí las palabras de 'El Matador'. La gran duda surge ante la posibilidad de que Gaethje decida retirarse, ya que la UFC tendría que elegir a dos peleadores para disputarse el cinturón vacante. La opción más mediática sería enfrentar a Pimblett y Topuria por ese cinturón, además de que Ilia es el campeón más reciente antes de Justin, pero Arman Tsarukyan ha afirmado que la compañía le ha prometido ser el siguiente que reciba la oportunidad titular. También ha aparecido la figura de Alexander Volkanovski, GOAT de peso pluma, que ha revelado que antes de retirarse quiere volver a subir a peso ligero para ser doble campeón. Dana White -jefe de la UFC- ha reconocido que no le puede negar la petición por todo lo que ha dado el peleador australiano a la promotora, de ahí que el peso ligero sea una incógnita a día de hoy. Lo que está claro es que la siguiente pelea de Topuria será muy mediática, con Gaethje y Pimblett como rivales más probables, por lo que todas las miradas estarán puestas en ver cómo regresa 'El Matador' después del momento más doloroso de su carrera deportiva.

articles.title: Gunjan wins second boxing gold for India at Youth Olympics with dominant 5-0 victory over Algeria's Bensalah
articles.summary: India's golden run in boxing continued at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games as Gunjan clinched the women's 48kg gold medal with a commanding 5-0 victory
articles.body: India's golden run in boxing continued at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games as Gunjan clinched the women's 48kg gold medal with a commanding 5-0 victory over Algeria's Bouthaina Bensalah in the final on Thursday. The Indian boxer dominated the contest at the Dakar Expo Center, with all five judges scoring the bout 30-27 in her favour.Gunjan maintained her composure and control throughout the three-round contest to secure a unanimous decision victory and add another gold to India's boxing campaign.The victory came after Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei had scripted history earlier in the day by winning India's first-ever Youth Olympics boxing gold in the men's 50kg category. He defeated Ireland's Kristian Jubani 3-2 in a closely contested final.Gunjan's dominant run to the gold medalGunjan enjoyed an impressive campaign in Dakar, maintaining an unbeaten record on her way to the top of the podium. After receiving a first-round bye, the Indian boxer began her campaign in the quarterfinals with a commanding 5-0 victory over Mexico's Atena Sofia Juarez Calero to assure herself of a medal.She continued her impressive run in the semifinals, defeating Great Britain's Lily Bassett 4-1 to book her place in the gold medal bout. The final against Bensalah proved to be another dominant performance from the Indian, who secured a unanimous 5-0 verdict to finish her campaign with the gold medal.Bensalah's journey to the finalAlgeria's Bouthaina Bensalah also produced an impressive run to reach the women's 48kg final. She began her campaign with a 5-0 victory over Thailand's Pemika Payungkasem in the round of 16 before defeating Nigeria's Shukurat Mayowa by the same margin in the quarterfinals.Bensalah faced her toughest challenge in the semifinals against Italy's Michela Guglielmon, eventually securing a narrow 3-2 split-decision victory to advance to the title clash. However, she could not overcome Gunjan in the final, settling for the silver medal after the Indian dominated the judges' scorecards.Ambekar scripts history with India's first Youth Olympics boxing goldEarlier, Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei created history by becoming India's first-ever boxing gold medallist at the Youth Olympic Games. articles.title: Eight people arrested after Abu Dhabi hotel brawl; Usman Nurmagomedov barred from RAF event
articles.summary: Abu Dhabi police say they have arrested eight people following a hotel brawl involving Merab Dvalishvili and Usman Nurmagomedov.
articles.body:
Abu Dhabi police say they have arrested eight people in response to the hotel brawl involving former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and PFL lightweight champion Usman Nurmagomedov, among others.

Video of the incident emerged online Wednesday , along with a video message showing a bloodied Dvalishvili claiming he was attacked from behind by Nurmagomedov and several other men.

According to a social media post by Abu Dhabi police , eight people were later arrested, including those who filmed the incident.

"The General Command of Abu Dhabi Police was able to arrest 8 persons involved in a fight that took place at the entrance of a hotel, on the background of previous differences between them, they also managed to arrest two persons who filmed the incident, take the necessary legal actions on their right, and refer them to the General Prosecutor to complete the proceedings in accordance with the laws enacted by it," said a statement posted to the official Instagram account of the Abu Dhabi police.

"The details of the incident go back to a fight at the entrance of a hotel, following previous differences between a number of people, and immediately, the Abu Dhabi Police specialized teams initiated their actions to deal with the incident, and they were able to arrest those involved, as well as arresting the two persons who filmed the fight, and taking the necessary legal actions for their rights," the statement continued.

"Abu Dhabi police stressed its keenness to maintain public security and order, and deal firmly with behaviors that would violate security or endanger the safety of others, stressing the importance of adhering to laws and regulations and civilized and responsible behavior."

The incident has also thrown into question the lineup for Saturday's RAF Abu Dhabi wrestling event. Dvalishvili is in Abu Dhabi to wrestle former WSOF bantamweight champion Marlon Moraes at Saturday's event. UFC bantamweight Umar Nurmagomedov — the brother of Usman Nurmagomedov, who could be seen slapping Dvalishvili at the start of the hotel brawl — is also slated to wrestle UFC Hall of Famer Urijah Faber at the same event.

Neither fighter was present at Thursday's RAF press conference, according to MMA Fighting , and RAF co-founder Chad Bronstein said he did not yet know what the status of those matches might be. Bronstein did say that, regardless of whether the matches move forward, Usman Nurmagomedov would not be welcome at the event.

"We're hoping that the situation gets resolved, sooner than later," Bronstein said on Thursday. "And obviously, Usman will not be attending our event on Saturday night."

The brawl involving Dvalishvili and the Nurmagomedov brothers comes after months of hostility between the two camps. Dvalishvili defeated the elder brother, Umar, in a UFC bantamweight title clash early last year. The two sides have engaged in a war of words ever since, though this week's incident was the most consequential clash yet, leaving several people visibly bruised and bloodied.
